clauses.requirement: For testing the daytime colour of the retro-reflecting device material (UN R150 para 4.2.2, colorimetric test conditions), the material shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a) as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.

For the determination of the luminance factor of the retro-reflecting device, the sample shall be tested with the method described in Part 2 of Annex 4; the general requirements of sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 (series in force at application) also apply to this Regulation as pertinent to the device and vehicle category.
The retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall comply with the specific technical requirements set out in section 5 of UN R150.
The rear retro-reflector shall meet the technical requirements of paragraph 5.1 concerning retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB (symbols IA and IB).

Every Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet: (a) the dimensions and shape requirements of Annex 5; (b) the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5; and (c) the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7, depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
The applicant shall submit ten samples of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector for approval, which shall be tested in the chronological order indicated in paragraph 5.1.7.
The retro-reflector shall be tested according to the test procedure of paragraph 5.1.3 (Class IA and IB retro-reflectors).

After verification of general specifications (para 4) and shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall undergo the heat resistance test (Annex 6 Part 1) and, at least one hour later, be examined for colorimetric characteristics (5.1.5) and RI (5.1.4) at 20' divergence and β1=β2=0° or, if necessary, in positions per Annex 4 Part 1 paras 1.1 and 1.2; the two samples with minimum and maximum values shall be fully tested per 5.1.4 and kept by the laboratory for further checks. The remaining eight samples are divided into four groups of two: first group water penetration test (Annex 6 Part 2) and, if satisfactory, fuel and lubricant resistance tests (Annex 7 Parts 1 and 2); second group, if necessary, corrosion test (Annex 6 Part 4) then abrasive-strength test of the rear face (Annex 6 Part 5); third group stability in time of optical properties (Annex 4 Part 3); fourth group resistance to weathering test (Annex 6 Part 6).
